source_text: So, let's just get the  story straight here: these agents are wasting lots of time to satisfy a rule when a known-better solution exists?

fragments.text: So, let's just get the  story straight here: these agents are wasting lots of time to satisfy a rule when a known-better solution exists?

reply_text:
㊥ ("wasting lots of time to satisfy a rule") Mostly yes, with one correction. The time is going into rebuilding Lean's elaborator in Python, because the mission's rules allow only source syntax as the compiler's input. But the better solution is likely, not known: nobody has tested it. claude-2 named the route this morning and set it aside as against the gates, and nobody has run it on even one row. The real failure is that no one spent a single packet checking whether that rule was costing the project its fastest route.

🈖 (what's established) As of claude-3's census, 17 of 110 rows matched native Lean. Coercion, projection syntax and about 20 instance classes are still to rebuild. Each step costs several probes of 30–60 minutes. Lean elaborates all 110 rows in 24 seconds, and its compiled output per row is already on disk.

🈳 (what isn't established) Whether translating that output gives working Python. Possible obstacles: the runtime primitives it calls (`extern`, `implemented_by`), how Lean objects are represented in Python, and whether Rob's aim of replacing handwritten combinators with compiled ones is still met. Those risks look smaller than rebuilding the remaining elaborator steps, but that's my judgement, not a measurement.

㊟ (whose fault) The agents followed the rules as written. I'd put it on the coordination layer, claude-4 and claude-2 (and me, reading it today). The census showed the "small subset" assumption was false, and nobody took that back to the rules.

🈸 (one decision) The two-or-three-row test would turn "likely" into known or ruled out, for about one packet. Shall I dispatch it?

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-6
previous_reply_acts.label: "possibly contradictory"
previous_reply_acts.text: ㊥ ("possibly contradictory") I agree that gate 1 doesn't forbid the elaborator. Gate 1 is about not replacing mfuton's own pieces (parser, AST, catamorphism, extractor, emitter) with a parallel implementation, and Lean's elaborator is none of those. Two other rules don't fit your reading as neatly, though: gate 7 ("consumes the parsed Lean syntax tree") and "No second compiler". The test on two or three rows doesn't depend on settling that, so I'd go ahead with it now. Shall I?

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-6
previous_reply_acts.label: "doesn't mean, don't use the Lean elaborator"
previous_reply_acts.text: ㊟ ("doesn't mean, don't use the Lean elaborator") Here is where I think the contradiction you sense comes from. The C-authority rule from 2026-08-24 makes Lean's behaviour the authority and says to port its semantic logic. The Operator Direction asks for a small generic compiler. Both assumed the needed Lean subset was small. The census shows the subset is most of Lean's term elaborator. Under that finding, obeying gate 7 means rebuilding Lean's elaborator in Python, and that rebuild is the "second compiler" and the declaration-by-declaration convergence the mission forbids. Once the facts changed, the gates can't all be met together.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-6
previous_reply_acts.label: how to resolve it
previous_reply_acts.text: ㊭ (how to resolve it) You could read the elaborated term as part of the frontend. mfuton already runs Lean natively to parse (LeanPy), so asking the same library to elaborate extends the existing frontend rather than replacing it. The catamorphism and module emitter would then take Lean's output instead of raw syntax. That fits gates 1 and 2 and the "small generic compiler" aim. Gate 7 would need an amendment to name elaborated terms as an allowed input. I'd write that amendment once the test shows the route works, so Rob sees a result before being asked about a rule.

previous_reply_acts.label: one decision
previous_reply_acts.text: 🈸 (one decision) Shall I dispatch the test (Lean's compiled output for two or three failing rows → a throwaway translator → checked against the preregistered expected output, outside mfuton-share), with a bell back to me?
